info.title: Leap Incentives — Lookups
info.description:
Partner-facing eligibility evaluation. Three operations, each its own sub-collection under the `incentives` resource:

  * `POST /v1.1/global-connect/incentives/lookups` — first-touch.
    Creates the customer if new, upserts devices, geocodes the address,
    resolves serving utilities, and evaluates eligibility.
  * `POST /v1.1/global-connect/incentives/refreshes` — re-evaluates an
    existing customer against their already-stored devices and cached
    utilities. No new customer or device rows.
  * `POST /v1.1/global-connect/incentives/overrides` — replaces the
    customer's device set with a new one (destructively wipes the
    existing devices), then evaluates against the new set.

The legacy `POST /v1.1/global-connect/incentives` path is preserved as a deprecated alias for `/lookups` so partners on the original release keep working. New integrations should use the explicit `/lookups` sub-collection.
`partner_id` is derived server-side from the authenticated principal's `leap-partnerid` header — it is intentionally not part of any request body. Accepting it from the client would turn these endpoints into an IDOR primitive over the customer / customer_device tables.

post.description: Pipeline: validate device IDs against the catalog → geocode the address (cached for 30 days per customer) → resolve serving utilities via PostGIS `ST_Covers` → upsert customer + customer_device rows + EAV attributes → filter candidate programs by (eiaid, customer_classification, device_category) → call the calc engine across all candidates → aggregate the per-program results into the partner-facing response. Persists one `incentive_lookup` audit row per call, sharing its `lookup_id` with the N `incentive_calculation` rows the engine writes for the same call.

200.description: Eligibility resolved (programs may be empty if the customer matches no candidates).

post.description: Loads the customer by `reference_id` (must already exist), reads the cached utility match + geocoded coordinates, and re-runs the calc engine against the customer's currently-stored `customer_device` rows. Does not create or update customers or devices. Does not re-geocode and does not re-resolve serving utilities — the cached values from the prior `/lookups` call are reused. Use this when programs, requirements, or spec versions have changed and you want fresh eligibility numbers for the same customer.

200.description: Eligibility re-evaluated using the customer's stored state.

post.description: Loads the customer by `reference_id` (must already exist), deletes every existing `customer_device` row for that customer, inserts a new set from `customer_devices`, and re-runs the calc engine. Reuses the cached utility match + geocoded coordinates from the prior `/lookups` call. Use this when the partner needs to wholesale replace a customer's device set — for example, a partner-side migration that re-keys installs or a teardown / re-install cycle. The wipe is irreversible within a single call.

Forbidden.description: You do not have permission to perform this operation

NotFound.description: Address is not covered by any utility we have territory data for. This is a coverage gap, not an internal failure — the caller should not retry.

Conflict.description: Conflict with existing customer state (e.g., reference_id already bound to a different address)

UnprocessableEntity.description: Request was syntactically valid but could not be processed (e.g., unknown device id, address could not be geocoded)

BadGateway.description: Upstream dependency (geocoder) is unavailable or rate-limited

reason.description: Human-readable explanation. Safe to surface to partners; no internal identifiers.

reference_id.description: Partner's stable identifier for the customer. The orchestrator uses this as the dedup key against `incentives.customer` scoped to the authenticated `partner_id`.

customer_devices.description: One entry per installation. Each carries the catalog `device_id` and an optional `partner_device_reference` that disambiguates two installs of the same catalog device. When omitted, the server assigns `"1"`, `"2"`, ... in request order, skipping any value already supplied by the partner. The inline `details` object accepts per-installation attributes (e.g. `customer_device.purchase_price`, `customer_device.installation_date`).

eiaid.description: Optional utility override. When supplied, the orchestrator bypasses both the geocoder and the geocode-driven territory (`ST_Covers`) utility lookup, and uses this EIA utility id directly to select candidate programs — useful when the partner already knows the serving utility and the address-based territory match is unavailable or ambiguous. On this path the address is NOT geocoded: the response `geocoding` block is omitted and the customer record's geocoded coordinates are left untouched. If no utility matches the supplied `eiaid`, the request fails the same way an un-served address does (404 `NO_UTILITY_AT_ADDRESS`).

customer_details.description: Partner-supplied per-customer attributes keyed by `requirement.key` (e.g., `customer.email`, `customer.is_homeowner`). The orchestrator persists these against the customer record and the calc engine consumes them during eligibility evaluation. Absent or empty → no partner-supplied attributes. Maximum 100 entries.

reference_id.description: Partner's stable identifier for the customer. Must match an existing customer scoped to the authenticated `partner_id`; unknown reference IDs return 404.

customer_details.description: Optional partner-supplied per-customer attributes to upsert against the existing customer record before re-evaluation. Use this to update values like `customer.is_homeowner` without touching the device set. Empty or omitted = no attribute changes.

reference_id.description: Partner's stable identifier for the customer. Must match an existing customer scoped to the authenticated `partner_id`; unknown reference IDs return 404.

customer_devices.description: The new device set for the customer. Every existing `customer_device` row for this customer is deleted before these are inserted — there is no merge step. The same `partner_device_reference` rules from `/lookups` apply (one entry per installation, server-assigned positional defaults when blank, uniqueness enforced within the request).

customer_details.description: Optional partner-supplied per-customer attributes to upsert against the existing customer record. Same shape as on `/lookups`. Empty or omitted = no attribute changes.

device_id.description: Catalog `device.id`. Must exist in the device catalog or the request is rejected with 422 `INVALID_DEVICE_ID`.

partner_device_reference.description: Partner-supplied per-installation identifier. Unique within the request. Echoed back in the response so partners can join their local records to the upserted `customer_device`. Server fills in `"1"`, `"2"`, ... in request order (skipping any value the partner already supplied) when omitted.

details.description: Partner-supplied per-installation attributes keyed by `requirement.key` (e.g. `customer_device.purchase_price`). Maximum 50 entries.

partner_device_reference.description: Server-resolved value (echoed verbatim if the partner supplied one; assigned `"1"`, `"2"`, ... otherwise).

country_code.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 country code. Defaults to `US`.

customer_devices.description: Per-installation echo. One entry per request entry, with the resolved (server-filled if absent) `partner_device_reference` and the upserted `customer_device.id`.

connect_url.description: Deep link the partner can hand to the customer to start the Connect flow. Encodes `reference_id` and (later) variant.

program_details.description: One entry per eligible (or conditionally eligible) program. Empty when no candidate programs match the (utility, customer_classification, device_category) filter.

upfront_amount.description: Always 0 in the current cut. Reserved for a future "pre-install upfront" payment kind.

install_amount.description: Sum across all eligible programs of incentives paid at install time. Maps from the engine's `up_front_total` per program.

ongoing_amount.description: Sum across all eligible programs of recurring incentives. Maps from the engine's `ongoing_total` per program.

operator_name.description: Name of the operating utility / agency. Currently null until the display source is wired in a follow-up.

display_name.description: Partner-branded display name for the program (PARTNER_OFFER rows only). Read from `program.metadata.display_name`. Null for non-offer programs.

logo_url.description: URL to the partner's logo (PARTNER_OFFER rows only). Read from `program.metadata.logo_url`. Null for non-offer programs.

terms_url.description: URL to the partner's terms-and-conditions page (PARTNER_OFFER rows only). Read from `program.metadata.terms_url`. Null for non-offer programs.

description.description: Free-form description shown to the customer (PARTNER_OFFER rows only). Read from `program.metadata.description`. Null for non-offer programs.

incentive_amount.description: Tier-level total across surviving devices. The calc engine produces a single scalar per (program, tier); per-device differentiation lives in `device_results[]`.

device_results.description: One entry per `customer_device` evaluated for this tier. Each shows whether that install passed/failed/ignored the tier's requirements and the per-check details.

partner_device_reference.description: Echoes the `partner_device_reference` from the request's `customer_devices[]` entry.

source_program_identifier.description: For Partner Offers, attributes the check to the program that produced it — the offer's `program_identifier` for offer-side checks, an underlying leap-defs program identifier for leap-side checks. Null on the existing rebate flow (INCENTIVES_DB programs).

IncentiveUtility.description: EIA-keyed utility identity used in incentive eligibility responses. Distinct from `common-schemas.yaml#/components/schemas/Utility`, which carries Connect's UUID-based shape with logo + connection URL.

CustomerClassification.description:
Customer/site classification used for incentive eligibility and flow routing.
Aligns with the leap-definitions canonical identifier `customer_classification`.
RESIDENTIAL/COMMERCIAL are the historic values; MULTIFAMILY and MANUFACTURED_HOME
are extensions for incentives eligibility (rebate qualification differs across
single-family vs multifamily vs manufactured housing).

BearerAuth.description: Your Leap API key as a Bearer token. Send it in the `Authorization` header: `Authorization: Bearer <api-key>`.
